sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1920) in Journal of Experimental Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2014) in American Psychologist extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Nancy Digdon, Russell A. Powell, Ben Harris (2014). Little Albert’s alleged neurological impairment: Watson, Rayner, and historical revision. History of Psychology.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2014) in History of Psychology extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Ben Harris (1979). Whatever happened to little Albert? American Psychologist.
sources.notes: Ben Harris's critical archival audit exposing textbook distortions of Watson and Rayner's 1920 single-infant conditioning report.

sources.citation: Mary Cover Jones (1991). A Laboratory Study of Fear: The Case of Peter. The Journal of Genetic Psychology.
sources.notes: Mary Cover Jones's 1924 counterconditioning reversal of childhood animal phobia via graded distance and food pairing.

sources.citation: Hall P. Beck, Sharman Levinson, Gary Irons (2009). Finding little Albert: A journey to John B. Watson’s infant laboratory. American Psychologist.
sources.notes: Historical archival investigation into the identity and clinical record of the infant filmed by Watson and Rayner at Johns Hopkins.
